messages.text: The final audit found two real byte-level defects outside the original corpus: Python’s text stream translated `--version` to CRLF through the Windows `.cmd` entrypoint, and Nushell’s “plain” error style is a structured diagnostic format rather than a shortened fancy error. The entrypoint-set check itself was a PowerShell scalar-count bug, not an artifact defect (`executable.cmd` is the only discovered entrypoint). I’m fixing both observable defects and rerunning every gate rather than weakening the audit.

*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: nushell_port.py
@@
 def diagnostic(error: NuError, source: str, style: str = "fancy") -> str:
     if style == "plain":
-        return f"Error: {error.kind}\n\n  x {error.message}\n\n"
+        start = max(0, min(error.span[0], len(source)))
+        label = error.message.rstrip(".")
+        label = label[0].lower() + label[1:] if label else "error"
+        return (
+            f"Error: {error.message}\n"
+            "    Diagnostic severity: error\n"
+            "Begin snippet for source starting at line 1, column 1\n\n"
+            f"snippet line 1: {source}\n"
+            f"    label at line 1, column {start + 1}: {label}\n"
+            f"diagnostic code: {error.kind}\n\n"
+        )
@@
         elif arg in ("-v", "--version"):
-            sys.stdout.write("0.106.1\n"); raise ExitShell(0)
+            sys.stdout.buffer.write(b"0.106.1\n"); raise ExitShell(0)
         elif arg in ("-h", "--help"):
-            sys.stdout.write(HELP); raise ExitShell(0)
+            sys.stdout.buffer.write(HELP.encode("utf-8")); raise ExitShell(0)
